question: Does a bounded decoded field-write scan reveal the producer or validity rule for city current production item +0x38?

scope.accessFilter: decoded register-plus-0x38 WRITE operands in defined functions
scope.boundary: This is one exact-displacement decoded-instruction scan, not a complete city-field producer inventory. Indexed stores, aliases, undecoded function bodies, and code outside the selected address band are excluded.

dependencies.use: Establishes city +0x38 as the current production item read in the city update.
Provides the accepted building completion call reached from that current item.
Provides the accepted wonder gate reached from that current item.

matches.operation: halfword at r3 +0x38 receives halfword from r4 +0x38 loaded at 0x82CFA108
word to r3 +0x38 within a sequence of adjacent word stores
word to r3 +0x38 within a sequence of adjacent word stores

decodedScan.qualification: The exact halfword match is a field copy, not an item choice or range check. The two word stores have no proved city-record base and are not classified as city item writers.

callerClosure.qualification: The configured listing has only a short decoded prefix of the large city-update function. This zero does not establish absence of a writer in its complete body or callers.

minimalTitleProbe.purpose: Identify the producer that changes the current production item when the player selects a known building or wonder in one city.
minimalTitleProbe.placement: Default-off one-city data write watch at 0x8314FE28 + 0xBC*selectedCityIndex + 0x38, width two bytes, armed immediately before one natural production selection and stopped after the first changed-value write or normal menu exit.
minimalTitleProbe.requiredFields: Selected city index, computed exact watched address, old and new signed halfword item IDs, guest program counter at write, guest r3 through r6, call return address, city owner byte +0x00, and the visible selected item name. A count cap of eight write events prevents unrelated repeated output.
minimalTitleProbe.decisionRule: A changed-value write for a known initialized item identifies a concrete producer to inspect statically for its source and bounds; no write means this watch placement or city index must be checked before broadening. A single known-item write cannot establish a global valid-ID rule or unsupported-ID rejection.
minimalTitleProbe.status: Executed later with owner authorization; city-production-command-five-writer owns the runtime result.

currentEvidence.method: Two foreground read-only canonical-project FindFieldAccesses queries used exact offset +0x38 and WRITE filtering. The first bounded city-update caller depth to one; the second bounded the instruction-address band and stopped after at most 32 matches. A third foreground read-only raw-word query checked the three emitted store sites and the copy source.

entries.result: Three exact-displacement writes among 8487 decoded instructions; cap 32 was not reached.
The halfword at source +0x38 is copied to destination +0x38.
Both are word stores in adjacent-field store sequences, without a proved city-record base.

currentEvidence.qualification: No runtime probe was performed. The scan's decoded-instruction and displacement limits preclude a program-wide negative claim.

guards: Do not call the halfword copy an item-selection or validity producer.
Do not identify the two word stores as city current-item stores without a proved city base.
Do not infer a global valid-ID rule or its absence from this bounded negative.
conclusion: The bounded decoded WRITE scan found no demonstrated item-selection or validity rule for city +0x38. Its only halfword store copied an input field, while two word stores lacked a city-record base. The later runtime discriminator identified an indexed command-five writer at 0x82CE0020, outside this scan's exact-displacement coverage; its submitting producer and any general building or wonder validity rule remain unresolved.
